title: Install an AMD Wraith Prism cooler without lifting it off its pre-applied paste
instruction: Install the CPU cooler on the processor. Once its thermal paste touches the processor, don't lift it off again or slide it more than 10 mm. Hook the fixed end of its clip over the lug first, then use the screwdriver to press the lever down until the loose end hooks over its lug, and swing the lever over the top until it locks.
context: Robots that build and service AI machines, from the GPU deep-learning workstations that system integrators and university labs assemble from retail parts to servers, fit CPU coolers with pre-applied thermal paste, and the paste only works if the cooler goes down once. AMD's installation guide: 'If you remove the heatsink/fan after initial installation, you must first clean the heatsink surface and apply new thermal interface material', and 'The heatsink must have full contact with the processor.' The Wraith Prism ships with the Ryzen 9 3900X used in many such builds, is still sold, and hooks onto the retention brackets every AM4 board carries (AM5 kept them). The finished install looks the same either way, so the paste rule is scored over the whole trial.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Motherboard: an ATX B550 board (e.g. MSI B550-A PRO; in simulation a 305 x 244 mm, 1.6 mm black board with memory slots, VRM heatsinks, M.2 heatsinks and an x16 slot), lying flat on the table and fixed to it, its long side along y, centred at (0.282, -0.064). Its AM4 socket is at (0.290, 0.000) with an AM4 Ryzen processor in it (e.g. Ryzen 5 5600; 40 x 40 mm lid, its top 9.7 mm above the table). Around the socket are AMD's standard AM4 retention brackets (black plastic, as shipped on the board), together 62 x 98 mm (x by y), with a lug on each end face at y = +0.049 and -0.049: 6 mm wide (x), sticking out 4 mm (along y), its flat underside 5.0 mm above the table and its top sloping from 9.0 mm down to 6.5 mm at its tip. Cooler: an AMD Wraith Prism (545 g, 93 mm tall): a 40 x 40 mm copper base with four 6 mm copper heat pipes and a 30 mm square of grey thermal paste pre-applied under it, a 92 x 84 x 56.5 mm aluminium fin block, and on top a 105 x 105 x 35 mm black plastic shroud with a 92 mm round opening, its fan 10 mm down in it. Its stock steel clip runs across its middle along y and ends in a strap at each end, 50.5 mm from the cooler's centre, under the shroud's edge, each with a 12 mm wide window near its bottom. The left strap is fixed; seated, its window spans 4.2 to 9.3 mm above the table, so the lug goes in sideways. The right strap is loose: sprung up, it hangs from the pivot of the stock black cam lever (48 x 8 x 4 mm), which lies against the shroud's right side, its pivot 66 mm above the base and 57 mm from the cooler's centre. Unlocked, the lever points along +x with its end raised 20 degrees; pressing it down pushes the loose strap down (7.6 mm of travel), and swinging it 180 degrees over the top, to point along -x with its end 20 degrees down, locks it, its cam pulling the strap tight; past straight up its spring takes it the rest of the way. The cooler stands on a dark grey foam support centred at (0.290, 0.200): a block 80 x 76 x 15 mm (x by y) with a 50 x 50 mm square hole through its middle. The fin block rests on its rim; the copper base and its paste hang in the hole, touching nothing, and the clip's straps and the heat pipes hang clear beyond the rim. The clip runs along y with the lever on the right, unlocked. Screwdriver: a Wiha PicoFinish 260P precision flat-head, 3.0 x 50 mm (150 mm long, an 18 mm round handle), standing tip down in a grey rack, a 30 x 30 x 28 mm block with a 4 mm square hole 25 mm deep centred at (0.220, -0.250), its 3 mm tip edge along x. Cup (empty): grey plastic, 46 x 46 mm outside, 53 mm tall, 30 x 30 mm inside, centred at (0.310, -0.250).
scoring: Tools: the trial video, two cameras, a ruler, and the paste print on the processor (seen when the cooler is lifted off for the reset). Paste rule, for the whole trial: once the base first touches the processor, it never lifts more than 3 mm off it, and its centre never moves more than 10 mm sideways from where it first touched, at any height in between. Setting it back down in place afterwards does not undo a lift or a slide. On real arms: a side camera on the board's far side, 80 mm from the processor and 16 mm above the table (just over the memory slots), looking along x, shows the lift as a gap between the fin block's bottom edge and the retention bracket's top (the 92 mm fin block as scale); a top camera and two 3 mm dots on the shroud's top corners show the slide from the frame where the base first touches; the print must be one square, not doubled or smeared more than 10 mm. In simulation both are checked on every control step from the cooler's pose. Seated: the cooler's base on the processor, its centre within 3 mm of the processor's, square with the socket within 5 degrees (the clip along y), tilted less than 3 degrees, base within 1.5 mm of the processor's top. The fixed strap can only be hooked then: lowered straight, it lands on its lug and holds that end about 5 mm up. Released: no part of the robot touches the cooler, and the screwdriver's tip is more than 80 mm (sideways) from the cooler's centre. The loose end is hooked when its lug shows through the strap's window and the strap hangs straight (within 1.5 degrees: in a side photo its bottom no more than 1 mm further out than its top), pulled up against the lug's underside. Locked: the lever has gone over the top and points along -x, its end down (turned more than 150 of its 180 degrees). 0 if the paste rule is broken, or the cooler is not seated (its fixed end hooked) or not released. 0.25: seated and released. 0.5: and the loose end hooked. 1.0 (success, held for 1 s): and the lever locked. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Swing the lever back over to point along +x, its end raised 20 degrees, unlocked; press it down and pull the loose strap out off its lug; slide the cooler towards the fixed end off its lug and lift it off. Before each trial, wipe the old paste off the processor and the base with isopropyl alcohol and a lint-free cloth, lay a stencil (a 0.2 mm plastic sheet with a 30 x 30 mm square hole) on the base, spread about 0.3 g of paste through it with a plastic card, and lift the stencil off. Stand the cooler on its foam support, base down in the hole, so that only the fin block touches the support; the paste touches nothing until the trial. Stand the screwdriver back in its rack and empty the cup.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; board fixed. The fixed strap is rigid; the loose strap slides on a spring (600 N/m) and flexes outward on another, and hangs from the lever, so pressing the lever down pushes it down. The lever's over-centre spring (past straight up) and cam tighten the clip. Shroud, fins and pipes are simple shapes at the Prism's sizes; the clip's and lever's positions are estimated from photos. Paste isn't simulated; its rule is checked from the base's pose.
